Maria: Heads up: ran a geo SLO sim this morning to exercise kernel handoff during region reroute. Short summary below, want quick eyes on the KV cold-start behavior.
Sam: nice — what harness did you use? synthetic or replay?
Maria: Replay harness with mixed client traces + a synthetic spike overlay. used seed 2026. configs: qps ramps, 1k concurrent reqs. Script:
```
./harness replay --trace=prod_week --overlay-spike=600s --seed=2026
```
Jordan: Where did the kernel switch happen? we saw a perf regression last week when we switched to fused-attn kernel.
Maria: Hand off occurred when requests hit fallback region (us-west1 -> eu-west1) after drain. Kernel auto-selector chose 'fused-attn-v2' in fallback. Observed p95 jump from 120ms -> 260ms for gen endpoints.
Alex: Was KV cache warm in fallback? cold KV can blow latency.
Maria: Yes — cache miss rate spiked to ~82% during first 90s. traced it to KV namespace not pre-populated because we didn't mirror runtime snapshots. Also batching heuristics collapsed under tail: batch size dropped from 16 to 3 with new heuristic.
Kevin: We should test pre-warm + pre-load + relaxed batching on handoff. Also check kernel selection thresholds; maybe fused-attn-v2 needs longer seq warmup.
Tasha: :eyes: I can run the SRE sim with network RTT emulation (+70ms to eu-west1) and TTL adjustments. Want quick patch in routing TTL to 30s?
Maria: Yes patch TTL 30s for sim. Also pushing a canary that forces 'classic-attn' kernel for fallback models to isolate kernel perf impact.
Sam: Results?
Maria: Canary + pre-warm reduced p95 to 150ms (still higher than baseline 120). KV pre-load nearly eliminated miss tail. Full logs:
```
perf-bot:bench/1792003456
```
Will upload flamegraphs.
perf-bot: Benchmark summary uploaded: https://redwood.internal/bench/1792003456 — p50/p95/p99, kv-miss histogram, kernel-switch traces.
Jordan: Looks like a perf regression correlated to a change in our kernel microkernel selector — commit abcdef. Can we roll that back on canary?
Kevin: We already reverted selector threshold on canary. Need a long-term fix: 1) prefer proven kernel under geo-handovers, 2) pre-warm KV namespaces, 3) modify batching heuristic to maintain throughput vs latency.
Maria: Agreed. I'll open a short RFC summarizing methodology + reproducible harness steps + recommendation list.
Sam: If you want I'll add an apples-to-apples comparison matrix (same seeds, same QPS, same model).
Maria: Please do. tagging @Kevin @Tasha for rollout plan. :thumbsup:
